interface.title: MetaboSpatial-CCI
interface.stage_of_work: Downstream analysis and interpretation of spatial expression data that has already been processed
interface.what_it_is_for: Infer metabolite secretion from enzyme expression, diffuse it with a reaction-diffusion model over the tissue spots, score metabolite-receptor interactions, deconvolve spots into cell types and build a cell-type communication network, starting from a spatial AnnData (.h5ad) file or a built-in demo.

data.note: Used the built-in demo dataset (500 spots, 500 genes, 50 metabolites, as shown in the header and Overview metrics). No .h5ad test file was available, so the upload route (Upload button, 200MB H5AD limit, 'Please upload an h5ad file') was seen but not used. The demo is not the same across server processes: app.py:219 takes list(real_genes)[:80] from a Python set, so which real genes get named depends on the hash seed. In this session every run gave 0 metabolite-receptor interactions and an all-zero hub table, and a KeyError: 'Mean Score' at app.py line 496 blocked the Interactions, CCI Network and Download tabs. The replay, using the same default settings, got 3 interactions, a non-zero Tumor hub and concentration values about 6× lower.

tree.general: Infer which cell populations communicate through secreted small molecules from spatially resolved expression data
tree.specific: Run the secretion → diffusion → receptor-scoring → deconvolution/CCI pipeline on an uploaded .h5ad or the demo Visium-like dataset, then explore concentration maps, interactions and hub cell types

The Net Secretion Rate map (red/blue, secretion + / uptake −) and the Predicted Concentration map (viridis) appear side by side, each with mean/max/min. Either map can be opened fullscreen. The exact patterns depend on the demo instance. In both runs Lactate was uptake only (concentration 0), and Adenosine's scattered secretion became a smooth central gradient. Prostaglandin E2 had a mixed sign and became a smooth gradient, but its peak was in a different place in each run (upper-left here, upper-middle in the replay)
